questions.worked_solution:
Let $g(x)=1-3x$ and $f(g(x))=g(x)^{8}.$ 

Differentiating, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(g(x)) & =({g}^{8})^{′}=8{g}^{7}, \\ {g}^{′}(x) & =(1-3x)^{′}=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the chain rule, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={f}^{′}(g(x))\cdot {g}^{′}(x) \\  & =8{g}^{7}\cdot (-3) \\  & =-24(1-3x)^{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=2x-1.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}={u}^{1/2}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2}{u}^{-1/2}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2x-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: The slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{4x+1}$ at the point where $x=0$ is{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=4x+1.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=4.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot 4 \\  & =\frac{4}{2\sqrt{4x+1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=0} & ={(\frac{4}{2\sqrt{4x+1}})|}_{x=0} \\  & =\frac{4}{2\sqrt{4(0)+1}} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
